chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: Why the band was not hired at the Palladium in the early fifties
summary: Machito says three bands were too costly for the Palladium and compares with the high cost of touring now.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Okay, Macho, you are very hot because I came out there, I remember that went over very big because of the double meaning and yet I hear from Mario Bauza that as hot as you were, you were flaming hot, you still couldn't work at the Palladium at that time. Why?
Well, it's no question that Tito Rodriguez and Tito Puente they had a good band and it wasn't enormously to have three bands.
Yes, always. Right now is the money, the ones that find problems. Let's say now all the big bands disappeared on account the expenditure in transportation.

As a matter of fact, we went to Chicago a few days ago and costs us almost five thousand dollars to go back and forth to Chicago. Now in top of that put accommodation. It costs about six almost seven thousand - about $8,000 to play one night in Chicago.
Okay, but I remember a time when there used to be the three big bands; Machito, Puente and Rodriguez and I used to get in for seventy-five cents before ten. I am talking about 1954.
